requirement.original: Why did session watcher trigger auto-restore when user manually archived a session? User says: manually archiving a session should not trigger restart.
requirement.clarified: The session watcher unconditionally restores any session that disappears from the running process list. It has no mechanism to distinguish intentional archive/kill from unexpected crash. A signal mechanism is needed so the watcher skips restoration for intentionally-removed sessions.
requirement.what: Add intentional-archive awareness to the session watcher so it does not auto-restore sessions the user deliberately archived or killed from the app UI.
requirement.why: Archiving a session from the app UI triggers auto-restore, which undoes the user's action, wastes resources, and spawns sessions under potentially the wrong daemon.

included: Signal mechanism for intentional session kill
Peak protection exclusion for archived sessions

success_criteria: Archiving a session from app UI does NOT trigger watcher auto-restore
Sessions that crash unexpectedly are still auto-restored
Peak protection does not resurrect archived sessions via merge
Signal files are cleaned up within 1 hour
constraints: Must work with the existing bash-based watcher
Must work across all 4 daemon homes
Signal must be written before process death to avoid race conditions
No network dependency in the watcher (server query is optional enhancement)

root_cause_analysis.symptom: User archives session 1140deaf from app UI. 60 seconds later, watcher detects 2 sessions disappeared and triggers full restore, spawning 10+ sessions under wrong daemon.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: watch_sessions() at line 642-644 of happy-session-recovery.sh triggers restore_online_sessions unconditionally whenever nr > 0 (sessions removed count). There is ZERO check for WHY sessions disappeared. The code: 'if [ "$nr" -gt 0 ]; then ... restore_online_sessions & fi' treats all disappearances as crashes.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: N/A - this is an original design limitation, not a regression
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: The watcher was designed purely for crash recovery. Intentional archive via UI was not considered as a disappearance scenario.
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: When a user archives a session, the CLI process is killed (via killSession RPC). The watcher sees the process disappear and immediately restores it, undoing the user's action. Peak protection then re-inserts the session into future snapshots, making it persistent.
root_cause_analysis.timeline: Always present since watcher implementation. Became visible when archive feature was added to the app UI.

development_approach.strategy: Implement a file-based signal mechanism. When killSession RPC is received, write a marker file (e.g., ~/.happy/archived_sessions/<uuid>) BEFORE killing the process. The watcher checks this directory before restoring each session. Peak protection also excludes UUIDs found in this directory. Cleanup removes signals older than 1 hour.
files_to_modify: /root/bin/happy-session-recovery.sh -- watch_sessions: check archived signals before restore; update_snapshot_with_peak_protection: exclude archived UUIDs; restore_online_sessions: skip archived; add cleanup_archived_signals function
/root/happy/packages/happy-cli/src/claude/registerKillSessionHandler.ts -- write archive signal file before calling killThisHappy()
/root/happy/packages/happy-cli/src/daemon/run.ts -- alternative: write signal in onChildExited when exit was RPC-initiated
development_approach.validation_approach: 1. Archive a session from app UI, verify watcher logs show 'skipping intentionally archived session'. 2. Kill a session process with SIGKILL, verify watcher restores it. 3. Check that archived signal files are cleaned up after 1 hour.
